previous.context:
This High severity Information Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write) vulnerability was introduced in versions 9.12.0, 10.3.0, and 11.3.0 of Jira Software Data Center. 
	
	This Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write) vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 8.7, allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to read files from the Jira web application root. 
	
	Atlassian recommends that Jira Software Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:
		
		Jira Software Data Center 9.12: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 9.12.40
		
		Jira Software Data Center 10.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.3.26
		
		Jira Software Data Center 11.3: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 11.3.12
		
		
	
	See the release notes (https://confluence.atlassian.com/jirasoftware/jira-software-data-center-release-notes.html). You can download the latest version of Jira Software Data Center from the download center (https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/download-archives). 
	
	This vulnerability was reported via our Bug Bounty program.

This High severity PrivEsc (Privilege Escalation) vulnerability was introduced in versions 10.2.0, 11.0.0, 12.0.0, and 12.1.0 of Bamboo Data Center.

This PrivEsc (Privilege Escalation) vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.4, allows an authenticated attacker to perform actions as a higher-privileged user.

Atlassian recommends that Bamboo Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:
 Bamboo Data Center 10.2: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.2.26

 Bamboo Data Center 12.1: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 12.1.13

 Bamboo Data Center 13.0: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 13.0.1

See the release notes ([https://confluence.atlassian.com/bambooreleases/bamboo-release-notes-1189793869.html]). You can download the latest version of Bamboo Data Center from the download center ([https://www.atlassian.com/software/bamboo/download-archives]).

This vulnerability was reported via our Penetration Testing program.

This Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write) vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.7 and a CVSS Vector of CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose protected application configuration files, which has high impact to confidentiality, no impact to integrity, no impact to availability, and requires no user interaction.

Atlassian recommends that Crucible Server customers upgrade to the latest version. If you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to the specified supported fixed version:
 Crucible Server 4.9: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 4.9.16

See the Crucible Server release notes ([https://confluence.atlassian.com/crucible/crucible-releases-298977378.html]). You can download the latest version of Crucible from the Crucible Download Archives ([https://www.atlassian.com/software/crucible/download-archives]).

The following description summarizes the vulnerability reported via our Penetration Testing program:

Crucible do not account for path parameters when validating protected paths requested through the static-resource route. A crafted path segment passes validation, after which Jetty removes the path parameter during dispatch and resolves the request to a protected resource. This can expose files under WEB-INF and permit direct invocation of admin-area JSPs outside the normal interceptor and administrative password checks. An ordinary authenticated user can exploit the issue, and unauthenticated exploitation is possible when anonymous access is enabled.

This Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write) vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 8.7 and a CVSS Vector of CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N allows an unauthenticated attacker to expose assets in your environment susceptible to exploitation, which has high impact to confidentiality, no impact to integrity, no impact to availability, and requires no user interaction.

([https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence/download-archives]).

The following description summarizes the vulnerability reported internally:

Confluence CssServlet forwards a request-controlled path to ServletRequest.getRequestDispatcher. The dispatcher URL-decodes and normalizes the path, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to use an encoded traversal sequence to access protected web application resources such as /WEB-INF/web.xml. previous.context: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. Prior to 1.38.4, any authenticated user can use the /api/configs/edit/{name}.json endpoint to modify protected configuration settings because ConfigsController::edit() does not enforce the System=Edit authorization requirement and its system-variable protection is ineffective. An attacker can set ZM_PATH_FFMPEG to a command-bearing value and trigger an exec() sink in web/views/image.php or web/includes/Event.php by requesting frame extraction. This permits arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the web server user and can expose private camera feeds, recordings, and database data or establish persistence. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.4.

previous.context: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.6.2 until 6.7, PATCH /api/config accepts unfiltered CivetWeb lua_* options through webserver.advancedOpts, while POST /api/teleporter writes attacker-controlled content from a dhcp.leases archive entry through src/zip/teleporter.c without content validation. An authenticated administrator can place controlled file content on disk, point a Lua execution option at that file, and rely on the advancedOpts configuration change to restart FTL. CivetWeb then executes the file as Lua through the processing in src/webserver/webserver.c, allowing arbitrary commands to run as the pihole operating-system user and persist across restarts while the configuration and file remain. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

previous.context: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. Prior to 6.7, log_http_access in src/webserver/webserver.c writes attacker-controlled User-Agent content to the access log without output neutralization when debug.api is enabled. If an administrator configures files.log.webserver inside webserver.paths.webroot with a filename matching lua_server_page_pattern, an unauthenticated request can plant Lua markup in that log and a later request can cause CivetWeb to evaluate the log as a Lua server page. The resulting commands run as the pihole operating-system user and can access or modify pihole-owned configuration, credentials, databases, logs, and rendered interface content. When the log is not served through the Lua handler, the same unneutralized writer still permits log forgery and downstream log-parser injection. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

previous.context: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, validation in src/api/list.c permits spaces for GRAVITY_GROUPS and consequently skips carriage-return and line-feed validation for group names submitted through POST /api/groups. The unsanitized name is copied into the Location value in pi_hole_extra_headers, and CivetWeb interprets embedded CR/LF sequences as separate HTTP response headers. An authenticated administrator can therefore inject headers such as Set-Cookie, Location, or Cache-Control; when a browser processes the response, this can cause session fixation, attacker-controlled redirects, or cache behavior changes. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

previous.context: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.30.0 until 0.40.3, an authenticated Agent with folder write access can use POST /upload to store HTML or SVG content that GET /download/{path} serves from the application origin through server/src/handlers/download.rs. The response sets Content-Disposition: inline and lacks forced attachment handling and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, allowing the browser to render the uploaded active content as the application. When a victim opens the link, the script can access the JavaScript-readable atomic_session cookie and the Agent private key in same-origin IndexedDB, enabling persistent account impersonation. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

previous.context: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. Prior to 0.40.3, unauthenticated requests to /bookmark can supply a url that server/src/plugins/bookmark.rs passes through fetch_data to fetch_body. Endpoint dispatch in lib/src/db.rs invokes the handler before check_read, and lib/src/client/helpers.rs previously checked only that the URL began with HTTP, without restricting loopback, private, link-local, DNS-rebinding, or redirect targets. The handler reflects fetched content in returned resource fields, making this a full-response server-side request forgery that can expose internal services and plain-GET cloud metadata. The short request timeout limits slow targets, and metadata services requiring a separate token request are outside the demonstrated GET-only path. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

previous.context: Filament Curator is a media picker plugin for Filament panels. From 3.0.0 until 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2, the Curator media panel accepts image/svg+xml files by default and stores and serves their markup inline without sanitization. An authenticated user with media-upload permission can store an SVG containing scripts, event-handler attributes, or javascript: URIs. When another panel user selects the View action, the SVG opens as a top-level browser document and its active content executes in the Filament application's origin. The script can perform authenticated same-origin actions as the viewing user and read same-origin data and script-accessible tokens. Panel thumbnails are not affected because they render through an image element that does not execute SVG script. This issue is fixed in versions 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2.

previous.context: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, check_client_auth() in src/api/auth.c detects that a matching session identifier has passed valid_until but still assigns user_id before the expired state can be rejected. An attacker who possesses a previously valid session identifier can periodically reuse it to preserve administrative access indefinitely, making the configured session timeout ineffective. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

previous.context: code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can submit an arbitrary PHP class name through the embed_key parameter to multiple embed API endpoints. The application passes the selected class to the Laravel service container, which invokes the class's __construct() method and recursively instantiates constructor dependencies, potentially causing unauthorized integrity or availability effects. The attacker cannot supply constructor parameter values or invoke an arbitrary method. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

The vulnerable path uses SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteEndpoint(); applications using SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteCallback() are not affected by this endpoint-selection flaw. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

previous.context: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264, the routes for PluginService::regenerateSecret and PluginService::delete carry no @Permissions decorator, and the methods omit plugin ownership checks. An authenticated attacker can directly target another plugin's identifier to rotate and disclose its OAuth secret or delete the plugin, including system plugins. Separately, PermissionGuard authorizes several nested API requests using a caller-controlled parent tableId, baseId, or spaceId, while the services resolve the requested child object only by its globally unique identifier. An authenticated attacker can provide a parent resource the attacker owns together with a victim's child identifier. ViewService::getViewById can then disclose another tenant's view configuration, embedded filter values, field layout, and shareId. DashboardService::updatePluginStorage and the view-position updatePluginStorage path can overwrite another tenant's plugin storage because the plugin installation is not rebound to the authorized base, dashboard, table, or view. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264.

previous.context:
The SOCKS5 client in subsys/net/lib/socks/socks.c built the CONNECT request in socks5_tcp_connect() by choosing the SOCKS5 address type from the address family of the proxy (proxy->sa_family) while reading the bytes out of the destination address supplied to connect(). A SOCKS5 request encodes the destination independently of the transport used to reach the proxy, so the two families are unrelated and nothing in the path forces them to agree: set_context_proxy() only requires the proxy family to match the socket, and zsock_connect_ctx() enters the SOCKS branch before any destination validation. With an IPv6 proxy and an AF_INET destination the code treated an 8-byte struct net_sockaddr_in as a struct net_sockaddr_in6 and copied the 16-byte sin6_addr from it, reading 12 bytes past the end of the object and transmitting them to the proxy.

With CONFIG_USERSPACE enabled, z_vrfy_zsock_connect() copies only addrlen user bytes into a stack-resident struct net_sockaddr_storage and enforces no per-family minimum length, so the oversized read stays within the storage but returns stale, uninitialised kernel-stack bytes. An unprivileged user-mode thread can therefore open an AF_INET6 stream socket, point setsockopt(SO_SOCKS5) at a proxy it controls, and call connect() with a short AF_INET destination to have the kernel send it 12 bytes of supervisor stack residue per attempt. Without CONFIG_USERSPACE the read runs past the end of the caller's own struct net_sockaddr_in, disclosing adjacent memory to the proxy; the family mismatch can arise unintentionally when a destination is obtained from DNS while an IPv6 proxy is configured.

Impact is limited to information disclosure of at most 12 bytes per connect() call, with no write primitive; the leak is delivered to whoever operates the SOCKS5 proxy. The mirrored pairing (IPv6 destination through an IPv4 proxy) is memory-safe but encoded the destination as SOCKS5_ATYP_IPV4 from the first four bytes of the IPv6 address, causing the proxy to connect to an unrelated host. Exploitation requires the non-default CONFIG_SOCKS option, a socket with SO_SOCKS5 configured, and both IPv4 and IPv6 support in the image.

The fix moves the encoding into a helper that selects the address type from dest->sa_family and validates dest_len against the matching struct net_sockaddr_in/struct net_sockaddr_in6 before copying, rejecting under-length or unsupported destinations with an error.

previous.context: Linkwarden is a self-hosted, open-source collaborative bookmark manager to collect, organize and archive webpages. Prior to 2.15.0, .github/workflows/check-branch.yml runs on the privileged pull_request_target event and interpolates the attacker-controlled github.head_ref source branch name unquoted into a run: shell script. An unauthenticated attacker can open a pull request from a fork with shell metacharacters in its branch name, causing arbitrary commands to execute in the base repository's privileged CI job before the branch comparison result matters. The job has access to GITHUB_TOKEN and any exposed secrets, allowing secret exfiltration and, when workflow token permissions allow repository writes, modification of repository content. This issue is fixed in version 2.15.0.

previous.context: Mistune is a Python Markdown parser with renderers and plugins. Prior to 3.3.4, parse_link_href performs an unbounded parenthesis-balancing scan to the end of the document for each unmatched opening parenthesis reached through an empty [] link label. In src/mistune/helpers.py and src/mistune/inline_parser.py, the empty label bypasses no_close_bracket_before, and no_link_before advances only past the short label, so successive [] ( candidates repeatedly scan the remaining document. Rendering untrusted Markdown with the default HTML renderer and no plugins can perform quadratic CPU work and keep a worker at 100 percent utilization. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.4.
